text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH: kubelet heartbeat skipped on 3 nodes in infer-usw-edge-n1 pool — pod evictions + GPU driver errors detected. paging oncall rota: mira (oncall)

mira (oncall): got the page. looking now. which nodes? any customer impact yet?

jess (sre): saw alerts for infer-usw-edge-n1-{a,b,c}. metrics show NotReady flaps ~every 45s, pods restarting, some OOMKilled logs from serving runtime. customers see 502 spikes.

ryan (infra): checking node health: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=infer-usw-edge-n1 -o wide` shows 3 NotReady. kubelet logs show repeated `Watch closed` followed by `failed to sync pod` loops.

devon (runtime): container logs from model-server show repeated `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED` and then `Killed: OOM`. sample snippet:```
E] cuda: failed to launch kernel: all CUDA devices busy or reset
W] evicting container due to OOM
```

sam (support): customer telemetry? support dashboard shows elevated 502 and increased lat p95 for a handful of heavy customers using long-context chat. will notify account teams if persists.

mira (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop scheduling to affected nodes (cordon) 2) attempt graceful drain for pods with fallback to cpu-variant 3) probe kubelet/journalctl 4) escalate if kubelet restart doesn't stabilize.

jess (sre): agreed. doing cordon now. `kubectl cordon infer-usw-edge-n1-a` `...-b` `...-c` :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: Action executed: nodes cordoned by jess at 4520001200.

ryan (infra): starting parallel drains with `--delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets --force` to move pods off GPUs. note: some stateful pods will failover slowly.

devon (runtime): enabling model fallback route for customer-facing route `text-gen-long` to route to `cpu-safe-1` for 10m. config snippet applied to routing policy.

mira (oncall): good — we need to free up capacity quickly. can we spin up extra dedicated capacity in eu-west to absorb traffic?

ryan (infra): provisioning 4 extra ded instances in eu-west, ETA ~3m. also pushing a quick agent restart to kubelet on nodes to see if heartbeat returns.

jess (sre): pulling kubelet journal: `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200` shows repeated error `failed to update RuntimeStatus: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = containerd: no such container` then `node heartbeats skipped` around same time as kernel logs indicate GPU driver reset.

devon (runtime): collecting dmesg: `NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00:00: Xid (Signal: 31, PID=0, Channel 00000000)` followed by `NVRM: GPU HANG` on all three nodes — looks like a driver/GPU reset race.

mira (oncall): that explains cuda errors. temporary mitigation: keep nodes cordoned + drain; restart kubelet after driver unload/load? careful — restarting kubelet alone may not fix driver hangs.

ryan (infra): plan: reboot nodes one-by-one after drain and verify driver is clean. I'll roll a reboot starting with `...-a`. executing now.

infra-bot: Reboot job started for infer-usw-edge-n1-a by ryan at 4520001325. logs: job-8843.

jess (sre): while reboots happen, toggled autoscaling policy to allow burst capacity in other zones. also temporarily increased max concurrent CPU fallback workers to reduce queueing.

sam (support): notified top 3 impacted customers with an incident note: "We're investigating GPU node instability that may affect latency and errors; we've routed traffic to fallback instances and will provide updates." :email:

mira (oncall): customer comms good. track which tenants hit fallback — need to reconcile cost/impact later.

ryan (infra): node `...-a` came back Ready, kubelet stable. verifying GPU status: `nvidia-smi` returns healthy, no Xid. starting to uncordon once pods reschedule fine.

devon (runtime): model server on `...-a` restarted and is `Running`. logs show no recent CUDA errors. re-enabling traffic gradually to that node.

jess (sre): repeating for `...-b` and `...-c`. note: on `...-b` we saw `oom_kill` for one large batch job — pods with large ctx were using aggressive batch sizes, evicted by out-of-memory. flagged runtime team to adjust batching limits.

devon (runtime): created emergency config to reduce batch_size and max_context for long-context route on GPU nodes until we finish driver stabilization. pushed at 4520001500.

mira (oncall): status check: 2/3 nodes back Ready, traffic mostly on fallback CPU + new eu-west instances. overall p95 improving but still elevated vs baseline. set incident severity remain SEV2 until fully recovered.

sam (support): customers acknowledged. support queue trending down. will escalate if any SLA breach.

jess (sre): root cause hypothesis: simultaneous GPU driver resets triggered by a bad kernel/driver combo + heavy batch jobs causing kernel-level GPU hangs, which made kubelet heartbeat time out and produced NotReady flaps. next actions: collect kernel + driver versions, open ticket with cloud vendor, plan a controlled kernel/driver upgrade sweep.

ryan (infra): capturing artifacts: `journalctl -u kubelet`, `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q`, `kubectl describe node` for all three nodes. saving to s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/4520001111/

devon (runtime): follow-up: add a canary config that reduces batch sizes automatically when GPU errors spike (auto-throttle), to avoid OOM cascades. filed RFC task INF-524.

mira (oncall): great. I'll handoff to jess for postmortem and follow-up ops items. jess — you taking handoff?

jess (sre): taking it. will run through post-incident checklist, assign action items: vendor ticket, driver roll, autoscale policy tweak, runtime auto-throttle. owners will be assigned in the doc.

mira (oncall): thanks team — unpin me when incident status moves to monitoring. closing page for oncall. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status changed to MONITORING by jess at 4520001958.

jess (sre): postmortem draft will go to #postmortems and link here. key immediate action: temporary bake warning on current driver image to prevent autoscaling into similarly configured nodes until vendor patch confirmed.

sam (support): final note: keep support loop ready in case customers revert to prior model.

mira (oncall): thanks all — end of thread.
